level: serious amateur aiming at professional competence

schools.name: Federal pipeline school
schools.optimises_for: competitive compliance — winning large, scored federal awards (Grants.gov, SAM.gov, 2 CFR 200) through rigorous process
schools.gives_up: long-term funder relationships and program flexibility once money is awarded

schools.name: Foundation cultivation school
schools.optimises_for: mission alignment and multi-year funder relationships (Candid, 990s, LOIs, site visits)
schools.gives_up: predictable process and fast decisions — foundations move on their own calendar

schools.name: Corporate sponsorship school
schools.optimises_for: brand alignment, speed, and low-friction awards from company giving programs
schools.gives_up: sustained general operating support — corporate grants are often one-off and project-tied

schools.name: Grantsmanship school
schools.optimises_for: the proposal as persuasion — reviewer psychology, narrative craft, and the scored document itself
schools.gives_up: portfolio-level pipeline discipline in favour of perfecting each individual ask

schools.name: Evidence-and-evaluation school
schools.optimises_for: demonstrable outcomes — logic models, outcome measures, and data-backed claims that survive scoring
schools.gives_up: narrative warmth and speed — evidence discipline slows every draft

clusters.name: Funder landscape
clusters.gist: Where the money actually lives — federal, foundation, corporate, and regranting pipelines — and how to match your work to a funder before writing a word.

clusters.name: Program strategy
clusters.gist: Shaping the work so it is fundable and measurable: problem, theory of change, logic model, objectives, and the evaluation plan that proves them.

clusters.name: Proposal craft
clusters.gist: The documents that get read and scored — LOI, outline, narrative, abstract — and the revision loop that makes them submittable.

clusters.name: Budgeting
clusters.gist: Turning the program into numbers that survive review: line items, personnel, indirect costs, match, and the narrative that justifies them.

clusters.name: Compliance & submission
clusters.gist: The mechanics that disqualify otherwise good proposals: registrations, eligibility, portals, deadlines, award terms, and audit readiness.

clusters.name: Stewardship & renewal
clusters.gist: Keeping the money once it lands — reporting, relationships, site visits, and converting results into the next ask.

clusters.name: Portfolio management
clusters.gist: Running grant-seeking as a system — pipeline tracking, calendars, win/loss learning, and capacity — instead of one proposal at a time.

nodes.label: Funder landscape
nodes.one_line: Sort any potential funder into the federal, foundation, corporate, or regranting pipeline and know which documents, timelines, and constraints each one implies.

nodes.label: Candid foundation search
nodes.one_line: Search the Candid Foundation Directory by geography, focus area, and giving history to build a real list of foundations that could fund your work.

nodes.label: Grants.gov opportunity search
nodes.one_line: Find every live federal funding opportunity relevant to your field on Grants.gov and read its synopsis before it closes.

nodes.label: Funder-fit triage
nodes.one_line: Read a funder's stated priorities, past awards, and restrictions to judge whether a project is a genuine fit before spending hours writing.

nodes.label: Prior-awards research
nodes.one_line: Pull a foundation's IRS 990s and recent grants to see who they actually fund, at what size, and for what duration — not just what they claim to fund.

nodes.label: Opportunity watch
nodes.one_line: Run saved searches and alerts on Grants.gov, Candid, and state portals so new and recurring opportunities reach you instead of being missed.

nodes.label: Opportunity scoring
nodes.one_line: Score a live opportunity on fit, odds, and cost-to-apply, then make a defensible go/no-go call for your portfolio.

nodes.label: Problem statement
nodes.one_line: State the problem your project exists to solve in one paragraph with named evidence, so a stranger reviewer understands why the work matters.

nodes.label: Theory of change
nodes.one_line: Write the if-then chain from your activities to the long-term change you claim, exposing the assumptions a reviewer will test.

nodes.label: Logic model
nodes.one_line: Turn your theory into the inputs-activities-outputs-outcomes table funders expect, with every column traceable to the next.

nodes.label: SMART objectives
nodes.one_line: Write objectives that are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound so your outcomes can be evaluated at closeout.

nodes.label: Needs evidence
nodes.one_line: Find and cite the statistics, studies, and local data that quantify the problem you opened your statement with.

nodes.label: Outcome measures
nodes.one_line: Choose indicators and data sources for each outcome so your proposal can claim measurable results, not intentions.

nodes.label: Evaluation plan
nodes.one_line: Write the who-measures-what-when plan, with instruments and analysis, that turns outcome measures into a fundable evaluation section.

nodes.label: Letter of inquiry
nodes.one_line: Write a one-to-three-page LOI that gets a foundation to invite your full proposal instead of passing.

nodes.label: Proposal outline
nodes.one_line: Map your full proposal against the funder's stated sections and page limits before writing a word, so nothing gets written that can't be used.

nodes.label: Executive summary
nodes.one_line: Compress the whole proposal into the one-page summary reviewers actually read first, hitting every scoring criterion in miniature.

nodes.label: Project narrative
nodes.one_line: Write the narrative body — need, approach, personnel, evaluation — that answers the funder's review criteria in order.

nodes.label: Review-criteria mapping
nodes.one_line: Walk your finished draft against the funder's published scoring criteria and confirm each one is answered with evidence, not implication.

nodes.label: Project abstract
nodes.one_line: Write the 250-word abstract that must stand alone in the funder's portal and win the skim.

nodes.label: Attachment pack
nodes.one_line: Assemble the supporting documents — org budget, bios, letters of support, financials — that reviewers check for capacity and credibility.

nodes.label: Revision loop
nodes.one_line: Run a structured read-through with a critical reader and revise against criteria and page limits until the draft is submittable.

nodes.label: Budget construction
nodes.one_line: Build a line-item project budget with personnel, fringe, travel, equipment, and other categories that sums correctly and tells the project's story.

nodes.label: Personnel & fringe
nodes.one_line: Price staff time with real salaries and fringe rates, allocating effort across funded and unfunded time so the budget survives scrutiny.

nodes.label: Budget narrative
nodes.one_line: Write the justification that explains each line item to a reviewer who wasn't in the room when you planned it.

nodes.label: Allowable costs
nodes.one_line: Check every line against federal cost principles and the funder's restrictions so nothing unallowable or disqualifying is requested.

nodes.label: Indirect cost rates
nodes.one_line: Calculate indirect costs using your negotiated rate, the funder's cap, or the 10% de minimis rate, and present them so they don't get cut.

nodes.label: Match & cost share
nodes.one_line: Identify a required match or cost share and document how it will be met — cash, in-kind, or third-party — before it becomes a compliance problem.

nodes.label: Multi-year budget
nodes.one_line: Lay out a multi-year budget with annual escalation and changing match requirements so the full award period is coherent.

nodes.label: SAM.gov registration
nodes.one_line: Register your entity in SAM.gov with a Unique Entity ID so you can legally apply for and receive federal awards.

nodes.label: NOFO deconstruction
nodes.one_line: Extract deadlines, eligibility, page limits, and review criteria from a Notice of Funding Opportunity so you plan the response before writing.

nodes.label: Deadline discipline
nodes.one_line: Work backward from a hard submission time to a writing and review schedule, and submit with margin instead of in the last hour.

nodes.label: Grants.gov submission
nodes.one_line: Assemble and submit an application through Grants.gov — forms, attachments, validation — without tripping the portal's rejections.

nodes.label: Eligibility check
nodes.one_line: Confirm your entity type, geography, and track record satisfy every threshold before committing hours to an application.

nodes.label: Award terms review
nodes.one_line: Review the notice of award's terms and conditions and flag anything you cannot commit to before you accept the money.

nodes.label: Regranting & subawards
nodes.one_line: Pass federal or foundation funds through to subrecipients with written subawards and their own compliance duties.

nodes.label: Single audit readiness
nodes.one_line: Track federal expenditures to the $750,000 threshold and prepare the documentation a single audit will demand.

nodes.label: Funder acknowledgments
nodes.one_line: Credit your funders in the places their grant agreements require — websites, materials, events — visibly and promptly.

nodes.label: Reporting calendar
nodes.one_line: Track every interim and final report deadline across active grants so no reporting window is ever missed.

nodes.label: Narrative & financial reporting
nodes.one_line: Write progress reports that document outcomes against the proposal's promises and flag problems before funders find them.

nodes.label: Funder relationship
nodes.one_line: Run a funder relationship deliberately — updates, transparency, responsiveness — so the funder knows you between applications, not just at ask time.

nodes.label: Site visits & check-ins
nodes.one_line: Prepare for a funder site visit or check-in so it confirms the story your proposal told instead of undercutting it.

nodes.label: Renewal & follow-on asks
nodes.one_line: Convert a completed grant into a renewal or expansion ask using reported results as the evidence.

nodes.label: Impact storytelling
nodes.one_line: Turn reported outcomes into a specific story with a named beneficiary that humanizes the grant for funders and boards.

nodes.label: Pipeline tracker
nodes.one_line: Keep a live list of every opportunity with status, deadline, and owner so you always know what's in flight and what's due.

nodes.label: Portfolio goals
nodes.one_line: Set a revenue target and funder mix for the year so individual proposals serve a portfolio, not a whim.

nodes.label: Win/loss debrief
nodes.one_line: Debrief every decision — win, loss, no-decision — and extract the pattern that improves your next ask.

nodes.label: Prospecting rhythm
nodes.one_line: Run a weekly scan-and-log habit so new funders enter the pipeline continuously instead of in deadline-driven panics.

nodes.label: Funding calendar
nodes.one_line: Build a 12-month calendar of recurring deadlines and submission windows so you plan proposals in seasons, not sprints.

nodes.label: Capacity planning
nodes.one_line: Match the pipeline to the hours you actually have, and say no to opportunities you can't staff to a competitive standard.

nodes.label: Revenue diversification
nodes.one_line: Shape the portfolio so no single funder or funding type is load-bearing for your budget.
